draft.title: What makes a referendum succeed
card: Very few referendums to change the Constitution have passed. Since 1901, only 8 of 44 have been approved.
Bipartisan support
the major parties back the change and campaign for it. When parties split, voters often hear reasons to vote No.
Public understanding
voters know what the change means and why it is proposed. Voters who are unsure tend to vote No.
Clear, simple question
the wording is short and easy to follow, so voters can see what a Yes vote would do.
draft.remember: Referendums are more likely to pass with major party backing, informed voters and a simple question.

a.q: Which situation makes a referendum more likely to pass?
opts: Both major parties campaign for a Yes vote
One major party campaigns hard for a No vote
Most voters have little information about the change
The question is long and has several parts
a.why: When both major parties back a change, voters hear one message and fewer reasons to vote No. A split between the major parties does the reverse, because it gives voters reasons to doubt the change.
a.clue: Think about whether voters hear one message or two.

b.q: A government proposes a change. Both major parties support it, but surveys show most voters cannot explain what it would do. What is the most likely result?
opts: It is at risk, because voters who are unsure tend to vote No
It will pass, because party support is all that matters
It will fail, because referendums need a unanimous vote
It will pass, because unsure voters tend to vote Yes
b.why: Party support helps, but it does not make up for voters who do not understand the change. Voters who are unsure tend to vote No. Party support is one factor, not the only one.
b.clue: Which of the three factors is missing here?

a.best: Both major parties campaign for a Yes vote

b.best: It is at risk, because voters who are unsure tend to vote No

problems.detail: 'Since 1901, only 8 of 44 have been approved' is out of date. The 2023 Voice referendum was the 45th, so the correct figure is 8 of 45.
The right option is the only hedged one ('is at risk'). The other three all predict a certain outcome ('will pass', 'will fail'), so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: What makes a referendum succeed
card: Very few referendums to change the Constitution have passed. Since 1901, only 8 of 45 have been approved, and success usually needs several factors at once.
Bipartisan support
the major parties back the change and campaign for it. When parties split, voters often hear reasons to vote No.
Public understanding
voters know what the change means and why it is proposed. Voters who are unsure tend to vote No, even when the parties agree.
Clear, simple question
the wording is short and easy to follow, so voters can see what a Yes vote would do.
proposal.remember: Referendums are more likely to pass with major party backing, informed voters and a simple question.
